tasks.task:
Plan two pieces of work from the owner's requests of 14 Nov 2026. The owner then said: "can you not just plan and drive that work?" So the decisions below are made; plan them as buildable milestones, not human decisions.

1) Code review fixes. A whole-repository review is at /Users/ryannel/Workspace/thrum/tmp/code-review-2026-11-14/CODE-REVIEW.md, with slices in sections/ beside it. Copy it into docs/evidence/code-review-2026-11-14/ and plan its fixes. The canonical shapes are already written in .agents/skills/thrum-engineering/references/patterns.md (review step 1); add the review's mechanical repo_check rules. Then follow its order of attack: confirmed bugs first (H01, H09, M41, H11, H14), then typed Rust-WGSL records and typed pass keys (T1, T2), test support and one GPU gate (T6), one device recipe and host core (T4), error convention (T3), performance (T12), and renames and splits (T9, T10) as one planned architecture milestone, then hygiene (T13). Give each fix to the module that owns the code, or a new module where none does. Modules are cut by isolation and ownership, and each delivers milestone by milestone in order; do not split CLOUDS or WATERS or change their milestones. Sequence work so it does not rewrite files that running builders hold (CULLING M3, APPLE-PRESENTATION M3, APPLE-TILE M10, CREATOR M3, EFFECT-GRAPH M3, ATMOSPHERE M9, CLOUDS M1, WATERS M1); later milestones of those modules may be rebased onto it.
   H03 decision: no Git history rewrite (it would need a force-push to main under many live worktrees). Plan the forward fix only: bulk media and archives leave the tracked tree under docs/ASSET-LIFECYCLE.md's storage rules (untrack at HEAD, keep selected small evidence), and repo_check stops new bulk binaries being committed. Keep evidence links that reviews depend on resolvable.

2) Separate the game from the engine. Owner: "it sounds like we're blurring the lines between the engine and the game a ton. Please let's separate out the game as much as we can, it shouldn't even sit in the same code base ideally." Today examples/v1-game (26k lines) holds engine host and shell code (host, window, browser, camera, projection, controls), engine qualification rigs (H20), and engine tests compile its source (H02/H13); thrum-cook depends on examples/asset-loop (H19); ARCHITECTURE places CLOUDS and PUDDLES selections in v1-game. Design the end state where the game lives in its own repository and depends only on the engine's public API: engine host/shell code moves into engine crates (also H15/M03), qualification moves into the owning crates or an engine-side harness, shared fixtures move to engine test support, and repo_check enforces the boundary. Stage it: first make the boundary real inside this repository, then move the game out.
   Repository decision: the game moves to a new local Git repository at /Users/ryannel/Workspace/thrum-games (v1-game now; the swarm game later), with no remote until the owner asks for one. It consumes the engine through Cargo path dependencies on a sibling Thrum checkout, so engine changes surface in the game at once; switching to pinned git revisions is a later step once the engine has releases. The last stage creates that repository, moves the game with its history-free copy, and leaves Thrum with no game code. The upcoming swarm game follows the same shape from the start. V1 still exits through the showcase game, so keep its milestones buildable throughout and say how the V1 gate is verified once the game lives outside.

Say which new milestones can start at once, and which wait for running builders.

Fix every Must Fix so the designs pass, resolving the GAME-SPLIT/TEST-SUPPORT interface conflicts together (one authority for each shared fixture). Keep the owner's decisions recorded in those plans: no Git history rewrite, the game moves to /Users/ryannel/Workspace/thrum-games with path dependencies, CLOUDS and WATERS unchanged. Retained device evidence outranks the review's suggestion where they conflict (REVIEW-RENDER MF1). Say which milestones can start at once.

Move Thrum onto the proof regime the owner approved, using orchestrate 2.3.1, in one pass, tonight.

Why: delivery stalled under proofs. In the last 24h, 4 milestones reached Ready for Review against 419 commits, and 163 of 288 background jobs failed. The single GPU lock was 92-94% busy, mostly with rebase, re-prove and merge attempts that failed. The design is in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ryannel-Workspace-thrum/e5ff9d25-dfb5-4b37-a169-158dbdac268c/scratchpad/proof-regime.md; section 4 has the steps T1a-T9. The script now does much of what it proposed: shared resources, lock hold limits, `reads`, a merge queue and main-branch checks with retry and bisect. Read ~/.claude/plugins/cache/ryannel-skills/orchestrate/2.3.1/skills/orchestration/build/SKILL.md, build-milestone/SKILL.md and plan-module/references/proofs.md before you change anything.

The owner's words, to quote wherever a change is the human's decision: "Ok, let's get the script and skill changes done then once we've got orchestrate to where it needs to be, let's get the lead on Thrum working." and "We want all these fixes in place before I head to bed tonight." The owner also confirmed "Go ahead" in the lead session on 15 Nov. That covered: a warning-only gate, an hourly verifier on main, `gpu: 2, chrome: 1`, BASELINE-GUARD re-planned, the rule and skill text updated, and accepting that an unintended image change can sit on main for about 2 hours.

Carry out, adjusted for 2.3.0:
- **T1a.** The exact-baselines gate in `./dev check` warns instead of refusing. Declare the verifier as a `Main-branch check` in ORCHESTRATE.md (every 1h; lock gpu; a timeout that fits the ~16 min run). Record a dated ruling in ARCHITECTURE.md's Exact baselines.
- **T1b.** The script now does the sentinel's shared run, retry, bisect and naming the culprit. Re-plan BASELINE-GUARD down to what remains Thrum's own (for example the verify command and the CPU ownership guard), and decide what happens to its in-flight M2 on branch build/baseline-guard.
- **Verifier items.** Open milestones carry about 116 items whose check runs `exact_baselines.py verify`. Changing `check` text resets progress, which `lock` and `reads` don't. Weigh repointing them at `python3 "$ORCHESTRATE_SCRIPT" main-check <name>` (no lock of its own) against having the verifier read the shared result. Pick the option that disturbs open branches least, and say why.
- **T2-T5,** as the report says. In T4, never nest gpu inside merge, and never hold a lock while waiting for a person.
- **T6.** Declare `Shared resources: gpu: 2, chrome: 1`; that capacity change is what ends most of the queueing. Give each item the lock its device needs for capacity. Use `gpu.alone` only for a run that needs the whole GPU, such as all its memory. It does not make timings trustworthy, because builders compiling elsewhere take no lock.
- **T9's timing policy is the timing fix.** Within a milestone, a timing item becomes a loose benchmark tripwire that catches a collapse. Precise numbers move to the module's last milestone, measured in one sitting with builders paused. Sweep the timing items to that line.
- **Fold T7-T8 in** where they're cheap; otherwise record them as later work.

Constraints:
- Don't edit the orchestrate skills or agent_loop.py. If the script blocks a step, stop that step and write down what happened.
- Keep open branches mergeable.
- Work in the lead worktree or your own; never touch the main checkout's tmp/.

Done when:
- the changes are merged to main, `./dev check-docs` passes and the plan checks pass;
- an open branch can merge without a fresh exact-image proof;
- the main-branch check is declared and `main-check --due` lists it;
- your report names the commits, every module whose design review is now owed, and anything you held back because it goes beyond what the owner approved.

Builders are blocking on the "no exact baseline moves" item. About 60 open items across 18 modules (CLOUDS WP7.9, RAY-TRACING WP4.10, SESSION WP5.10, WATERS WP13.13, RENDER-2D WP3.11 and WP3.13, GAME-SPLIT, GAME-UI, PUDDLES, RIVERS, SWARM, SHOWCASE and others) check with `python3 scripts/exact_baselines.py verify`, which without --full delegates to `agent_loop.py main-check exact-images`; orchestrate refuses any item check that invokes main-check, so each of those work packages blocks (CLOUDS WP7 and RAY-TRACING WP4 have, and REPO-RULES WP5 already had its copy removed). Fix this once for the whole project rather than per module.

The lead's assumption, which the owner can overturn: the registered main-branch check `exact-images` (ORCHESTRATE.md) already guards that no baseline moves after every merge, and the owner wants fast merges with long proofs on main, not in each work package. So remove these items where nothing else in the work package depends on them, or replace them with something the work package can show before the merge, such as a check that it changed no registered baseline or comparison file. Do not make each work package run `verify --full`. Change scripts/exact_baselines.py in its owning module only if that is the cleaner fix. Put CLOUDS WP7 and RAY-TRACING WP4 first, since their builders have finished and wait only on this.
